tools.name: get_my_profile
tools.description: Return the signed-in user's own EQIQs profile: results across the 21-framework battery (MBTI, Big Five, Enneagram, DISC, EQ and more), plain-language labels, and which frameworks are still missing. Use when the user asks about themselves, e.g. 'what is my Enneagram type?' or 'how do I come across at

tools.name: list_profiles
tools.description: List the people saved in the signed-in user's EQIQs workspace (id, name, department, how many of 21 frameworks are complete). Use to find someone before calling get_profile, score_compatibility or score_team. Read-only; costs 1 unit.

tools.name: get_profile
tools.description: Return the full 21-framework read for one saved person: results per framework with plain-language labels, strengths, and working-style notes. Provide exactly one of profile_id, email or name. Read-only; costs 1 unit.

tools.name: create_profile
tools.description: Add a new person to the user's workspace, optionally with traits already known (e.g. an MBTI type from a past assessment). Use invite_person instead when the person should take the assessment themselves. Returns the new profile id. Costs 1 unit.

tools.name: list_relationships
tools.description: List compatibility pairings the user has already saved, with each pair's score and the context it was scored in. Use to recall earlier comparisons without re-scoring. Read-only; costs 1 unit.

tools.name: score_compatibility
tools.description: Score how two people work (or relate) together, 0-100, with a visual score card, sub-scores (communication, values, conflict and more), why the score landed where it did, and practical tips. Use for one pair; use score_team for three or more. Decision-support only, never the sole basis for hiring, p

tools.name: add_note
tools.description: Save a private note or check-in on one person in the user's workspace; it appears on their EQIQs profile. Use after 1:1s or when the user asks to remember something about someone. Costs 1 unit.

tools.name: list_notes
tools.description: Read the user's saved notes and check-ins on one person, newest first. Use before a 1:1 or with prep_meeting. Read-only; costs 1 unit.

tools.name: invite_person
tools.description: Create a private invite link for someone to take the EQIQs assessment and compare with the user. Finishing the assessment is their consent to share results. Optionally emailed by EQIQs; otherwise the link is returned to hand over. Limited to 10 invites per hour; no self-invites or opted-out addresse

tools.name: list_invites
tools.description: List comparison invites the user has sent and each one's status: pending, clicked, started or completed. Read-only; costs 1 unit.

tools.name: score_team
tools.description: Score a whole group in one call: every pairing is rolled up into a team cohesion score (visual card), the weakest shared dimension, the best-connected person, who is most isolated, pairings to watch (<55) and anchor pairings (75+), and the role mix with what is missing. Use instead of looping score_

tools.name: start_assessment
tools.description: Get the questions for one EQIQs framework so the user can take it inside the chat. Ask them one at a time, word for word, accepting only A or B. Call with no framework to list what the user has not completed yet. Personal frameworks (attachment, love language) need the user's explicit consent. Read-

tools.name: submit_assessment
tools.description: Score the answers collected via start_assessment with EQIQs' own scoring and save the result to the signed-in user's profile (overwrites an earlier result for that framework). Returns the result in plain language. Costs 1 unit.

tools.name: prep_meeting
tools.description: Build a meeting prep brief for 1-12 attendees: how to communicate with and persuade each person, and which pairings in the room need care. Name attendees or pass a department. Read-only; costs 2 units.

tools.name: suggest_lead
tools.description: Rank 2-12 people for leading a kind of work (execution, people, innovation or analysis), showing the saved results behind each ranking and any thin data. Use for 'who should lead this project?'. Decision-support only. Read-only; costs 2 units.

tools.name: generate_narrative
tools.description: Premium: write a plain-language coaching narrative for one person, or for a pair when compare_with is given, synthesized from all 21 frameworks. Business context stays on working behavior only. Slower than other tools. Costs 5 units.

findings.title: Read-only tool requests dangerous parameters
findings.detail: Tool "get_my_profile" appears informational but accepts parameters (context) that enable code/file/secret access.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "list_profiles" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: List the people saved in the signed-in user's EQIQs workspace (id, name, department, how many of 21 frameworks are complete). Use to find someone before calling…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp-server" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_profile, start_assessment · Private data: add_note, invite_person · Public sink: get_profile, invite_person, submit_assessment.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_profile, start_assessment · Private data: add_note, invite_person · Public sink: get_profile, invite_person, submit_assessment

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "get_my_profile" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
